A Block contains one to three planned groups. Defeat every group to link the Block. Each cleared group earns 50 points once.
A bribed broker diverted a Dark Delta shipment to a shadow fleet. After paying for the betrayal, its funds barely covered spare parts. Very few stolen hulls received better equipment.
A hostile blockade intercepted returning Sky Breakers. Maintaining the blockade consumed its funding, so captured ships usually continued with the equipment they had launched with.

Advanced and Elite ship stages add protection against enemy projectiles per life. A ship collision still needs a shield to be absorbed.
Advanced and Elite ship stages, armor and new start power-up purchases are marked MAINNET READY. Previously owned items remain usable.
Advanced carriers connect distributed knowledge depots. Several custodians accompany every handover.
Advanced couriers carry verified aid pledges between clinics. Their old racing numbers preserve their shared origin.
Advanced couriers protect scheduled exchanges at the outer rings. No promised meeting should pass without a message.
Advanced crews come from both home ports. Their joint logs preserve disagreements as well as decisions.
Advanced formations escort independent messengers across closed borders. They carry multiple sources rather than one prescribed truth.
Advanced formations verify reopened trade routes. Every course bears several navigators’ signatures.
Advanced pilots guard the couriers carrying those charts onward. Their insignia depicts the first mapped star.
Advanced ships carry repair knowledge into emergency zones. Their red markings stand for urgent assistance.
Advanced ships escort disputed cargo to joint inspection. Their records remain available to both sides.
Advanced ships secure exchanges between greenhouse stations. Their identifiers preserve the names of forgotten plants.
Advanced ships secure meetings between independent delegations. Their escort ends at both home ports.
Advanced squadrons escort pioneer convoys on their first shared voyages. Their identifiers remember the contributing workshops.
Advanced squadrons maintain contact with drifting research stations. Their callsigns follow the ring’s old meeting points.
Advanced units guard mobile workshops during difficult recoveries. Their pilots know the repair teams’ emergency signals.
Advanced watches escort supplies through prolonged radio silence. Their shifts take the names of rescued ships.
After all turrets explode, a concealed central weapon opens. Attack the now vulnerable hull and dodge its pulses.
After Block 9, the boss arrives. Defeat it to enter the bonus round; the next level begins with a fresh chain.
After breaking a truce, a hostile delegation kept borrowed Olive Fortresses. Neutral backers froze all funding. Replacing failed parts then took priority over upgrades.

After occupying a shipyard, attackers forced its remaining workers to restore old Iron Guards. They lacked both money and suppliers for new weapons, so most stolen hulls retained their original specification.
Aimed single shots alternate with a four-shot fan.
Aimed single shots alternate with a two-shot fan.
Akraveth settled disputes between distant trading posts. Its chamber once compared evidence and sought fair outcomes. The shadow fleet replaced its judges with a system of predetermined verdicts.
An active shield also protects against shots and ship collisions. Timed weapons and power-ups are collected or purchased separately and are not included in this upgrade.
An enemy extortion group seized Red Comets under a false repossession order. The colonies stopped paying. Without the expected income, most captured rescue ships remained technically unchanged.
An indebted mapping company sold retired Nova Wings to an enemy front dealer. His sponsors could afford the hulls but few new weapons, leaving most in their original configuration.
An occupied customs depot supplied the enemy with Cargo Hawks. Instead of treasure, the holds contained mostly sealed evidence. The poor proceeds could not fund a major refit of the captured fleet.
An older weapon selection is saved but no longer activates automatically. Every mission starts with the single laser.

Archive raiders captured Core Carriers hoping to sell their knowledge. Distributed keys rendered the stolen archives worthless. Disappointed patrons withdrew, making expensive upgrades a rare exception.
Armor is always active from mission start, needs no shield and remains yours across all future missions. Each upgrade adds to your maximum hearts.

At level 1, defeats earn Shards by enemy class: light 2, medium 4–5, elite 6, heavy 8, boss 16. Rewards grow with level. Bonus targets earn 1 each, plus a completion reward that grows with level. The HUD shows your previous Shard balance plus this mission's earnings.
Attackers stole several Night Guards during a watch change. Their sponsors paid for the raid, not long-term upkeep. Most captured ships therefore remained basic patrol models.
Available only as a weapon pickup on Testnet.
Available only as a weapon pickup.
Avoid enemy ships and projectiles. An active shield absorbs an impact; otherwise a collision or an unguarded projectile can cost a heart.
Awards are saved to your Pi account immediately. Admin test runs do not count.
Azhrel mapped the first jump connections through the nebula frontier. Its charts saved countless convoys. Captured by hostile commanders, those trusted maps became unusually convincing traps.
Azravel searched for lost colony probes where few rescuers travelled. Its help once reached forgotten places. Today it targets stations that have just lost data or access.
between volleys when projectile slots are available.
Bosses have their own silhouettes, weapon turrets and engine positions. Their appearance differs from the normal ships.
Build your streak, master the grid, and become the force Earth needs.
Career Score adds verified completed runs. Best Run is the highest single run with its reached level. Profile level is separate. Earlier records remain in the previous lists.

Cargo Hawk originated in a harbour whose small tugs were often overlooked. When a fraud ring forged receipts, their crews collected independent logs and brought them together despite threats. The new hull took its name from that courier alliance. In its legend, the most important cargo is complete evidence of rightful ownership.
Central weapon: pulse, calibre 8. Initial warning 1.8 s; then {value0} s volley interval.
Choose a topic to learn the current rules before your mission.
Collect the heart to start the bonus round.

Collected weapon upgrades activate immediately. If another timed weapon is available, its own side button lets you switch between them. Previously owned start boosts have a separate activation button.
COLLECTOR CARD · Fiction from the Cryptoid universe / actual game stats · Edition 01

Colonies argue over conflicting claims while the ship reaches another market. The deception concerns provenance, not the value of shared knowledge. Drelkash defends its moving forgery workshop fiercely. Its defeat reconnects the records with the history they actually came from.
Combat progress is saved to your Pi account. Older saves resume at the last completed Block.
Combo rewards are already included in your score and earned Shards. The bonus-round and mission summaries show the earned totals without crediting them again.
Complete chains in different levels to earn milestones at 1, 3, 10, 25 and 50 chains. The best bonus medal for each level is shown in your collection.
Complete this activity to earn points
Completed blocks stay saved. The current section restarts when you return.
Completed sections stay saved in your Pi account. An unfinished section restarts when you resume.
Completed sections stay saved. Your remaining lives are kept when you leave.
Connect your Pi account to see your saved loadout.
Continuous protection for 60 seconds after activation. The timer pauses during mission transitions.

Contradictory warnings make traders abandon safe routes and colonies distrust their partners. No rumour needs to last: another is already on its way. Veshkorn protects a factory of uncertainty. Its defeat makes room for verifiable information instead of an endless race against the next manufactured panic.

Core Carrier was built when several colonies needed to safeguard their final knowledge archives. Each contributed a store, but none was to control the collection alone. The crew maintained separate provenance records and shared catalogues. The design represents carrying others’ knowledge without claiming it: its purpose is the next safe handover.

Cryptoid Evolution is an arcade space shooter. Pilot your ship, defeat formations and bosses, collect boosts and build your fleet.
Damaged turrets glow intense orange before exploding.

Dark Delta was never built for glory. Its first mission was to search silent outposts for survivors. Early logs contain more coordinates than names because crews protected the rescued settlers’ privacy. A tradition grew from that choice: success is measured by who returns safely, not by who tells the story.
Defeated enemies earn points and in-game Shards. The HUD shows your previous Shard balance plus this mission's earnings.
Defectors delivered several Twin Cores to an enemy fleet. Both original shipyards then refused further supplies. Replacements became expensive, and the new owners cut almost every planned upgrade.

Deliveries remain in limbo while each community believes the other is withholding them. Zorveth draws power from that misunderstanding. Its hull is the visible border of an invisible dispute. The defenders must open the passage without turning one colony against the other.
Destroy every turret first. The central weapon then opens; the hull becomes vulnerable and takes double damage.
Destroy every turret first. The hull then becomes vulnerable and takes double damage; the central special weapon opens.
Different enemy classes pay different amounts. Linking all nine Blocks awards a chain reward, and beating the boss awards more.
Discover 50 bosses and 60 ship cards. Each unlocked card tells its story and can be saved with its equipment as a PNG.

Dornavik recovered damaged data stores from burning wrecks. Its insulated chambers once kept records alive when everything around them failed. The shadow fleet recognised a ship able to reach archives others could not.

Dorzheva recovered personal logs from wrecked freighters and returned them to families. Its holds were filled with small, precious histories. Under new command those memories became instruments of targeted deception.

Dravosk replaced failed communication stations in empty regions. Its visible antennas promised connection where none remained. Today it welcomes incoming signals but forwards them only according to its patrons’ interests.

Drazevorn was assembled from abandoned command decks. Its archives unite the earlier enemies’ deceptions: stolen names, false chronicles and sealed evidence. It symbolises an order in which one voice alone decides what is true.
Drazkell supplied navigation buoys with tiny energy deliveries. Its holds were designed for millions of small transfers. Hostile commanders repurposed that capacity for a quiet surveillance campaign.

Drelkash preserved rare star charts by making clearly labelled copies for schools and navigators. Its workshops helped knowledge travel. Today its crew removes the labels and sells every copy as a unique original.
Drelvorn was a travelling vault for the seals of old fleet commanders. During a rebellion its guardian system locked out the rightful custodians and departed with their credentials.
During a network outage, enemies occupied a remote hangar full of Storm Wings. Severed supply lines made every replacement costly. Their limited budget usually covered operation, not advanced refits.
During the reactor weapon phase, small escorts return in waves. The pauses shorten as levels rise; from level 50, the next wave enters as soon as the previous one is cleared.
Each Block is one encounter: enemies enter, form a recognizable pattern and break away for attack runs. Defeat the formation to link that Block.
Each level has nine visible Blocks, then a boss fight and a bonus round.
Each signed-in Pi player appears once with their highest completed run. Guests keep a local best on this device.
Elite formations defend the new solar stores against the shadow fleet, protecting the light the refugees managed to carry away.
Elite pilots protect major repair convoys after outages. Their return means help has found a route again.
Elite pilots protect the shared observation archive from falsified readings, preserving years of independent research.
Elite pilots recover witnesses whose accounts can reconcile entire colonies. Their reputation rests on discretion rather than spectacle.
Elite ships cover the withdrawal of final salvage teams. Their honours name the workshops that survived to work again.
Elite ships defend the rebuilding of shattered stations. Their honours recognise shipyard crews brought to safety.
Elite ships guard the great gatherings of travelling colonies. Their arrival announces a connection renewed.

Enemy crews took abandoned Solar Lances when an evacuation base fell. Their supply budget mainly funded escape routes for commanders, leaving captured vessels with makeshift repairs rather than upgrades.
Enemy groups copied old Pi Vanguard plans and took over decommissioned hulls. They lacked funding for newer precision assemblies, leaving their small fleet largely in its early configuration.
Enemy hulls have different strengths. Even the first boss needs sustained fire; bosses attack faster as their hull weakens.
Enemy mercenaries accepted Striker hulls from an insolvent employer. Resale brought too little, so some kept the ships. Few crews could afford a substantial refit.

Engagement is a broad concept, like visiting the app to taking specific actions within its interface. In the future, individual apps will guide you through the specific interactions that define their unique engagement criteria.
Every defeat counts in only one pair. Four simultaneous defeats earn two combos; an unpaired third defeat can start the next pair. Combos also apply in boss battles and bonus rounds.

Every displaced trail protects another shadow-fleet shipment. Honest traders fall under suspicion while the culprits change names. Its armour guards the remaining originals. The defenders must secure that archive before the origins of entire fleets become nothing more than convincing stories.
Fiction from the Cryptoid universe. Does not add combat abilities.
Five to eight hits earn a bronze medal, nine to eleven silver, and all twelve gold. A perfect round can also restore one lost heart.
Fly through glowing drops to collect boosts that activate immediately.
For this assignment, the Advanced refit adds permanent twin fire and protection against one enemy projectile hit per life to the base hull.
Forged freight contracts transferred a number of Vectors to enemy owners. When the fraud was uncovered, their funding stopped. Reserves kept the ships flying but paid for few upgrades.
Free boosts can appear throughout the campaign, but each type appears only once per level.

Gold Streak began in races between trading moons. During a supply crisis its pilots used their route knowledge to carry medical records past closed harbours. A sporting league became a courier union. The golden markings recall the thin sunlight between moons that guided its first couriers, rather than wealth.
Grey Scout is free; nine Standard hulls cost Shards. Other hulls are currently locked.
Grey Scout is free. Use earned Shards for available Standard ships and their color variants.
Guest ship cards are stored on this device. Sign in to view your account collection.
Hangar catalog unavailable. Try again when the server is online.
Hostile gangs confiscated Gold Streaks on a deserted racing moon. They expected prize money, but the races had ended long before. Without that income, they seldom modernised their new fleet.
HP means game health; calibre is a relative game value. Volley delays apply to intact turrets; targeting and the shared projectile limit may extend them.
Hull protection absorbs {value0} enemy projectile hits per life. It does not protect against direct ship collisions.
Import not confirmed. Check your account inventory in the hangar.

In its fictional history they become remotely controlled transmitters overwhelming entire regions with simultaneous requests. Their owners barely recognise their own machines. Destroying Thalzek ends the swarm’s command post in this story. Its actual mounted combat weapons are recorded separately, without inventing extra battle abilities.
In System, choose language, touch-control side, sensitivity and ship start height. Music, effects volume and reduced visual effects have their own controls.

Irdavoss once synchronised the clocks of frontier stations. Entire fleets timed their manoeuvres to its precise broadcasts. After a silent change of command, the signals stayed clear but their readings became false.

Iron Guard was designed by dock workers unwilling to leave their home’s defence to outside fleets. Its first hull used parts from retired cargo cranes. The keel bore the names of people who worked on it after their shifts. The series remembers that defence can mean caring for a place built by many hands.
IRRA pricing is for demo purposes.

It blocks agreements with fresh objections and gives each side different supposed conditions. While colonies argue, hostile ships occupy their routes. Keldroth attacks the ability to act together at all. Its defeat provides time to distinguish genuine differences from obstacles manufactured to prevent any resolution.

It confirms that records exist while withholding their contents. Investigators can see a claim but cannot examine the evidence themselves. Korthaven turns visibility into an empty assurance. Defeating it restores the access without which even a beautiful ledger is only a list of unreachable promises.

It constructs convincing messages from familiar details and approaches victims with knowledge of their past. Its danger lies in the closeness it pretends to offer. Dorzheva guards a collection of stolen familiarity. Defeating it prevents the traces of a life from being turned against their owner.

It declares counterfeit inspections successful and grants unsafe counterparties the appearance of official approval. Colonies trust its stamps until deliveries vanish. The defenders must expose the deception behind its venerable name: confidence needs verifiable responsibility, not merely an old emblem on an armoured hull.

It displays invented inspection results and attractive security seals where independent checks are absent. The forgery lies in the claimed certainty itself. Kelzorn keeps investigators away with its weapons. Its defeat reveals what its owners fear most: a second, independent look behind a reassuring surface.

It distributes altered maintenance packages meant to make other ships dependent on the shadow fleet. Failures often appear only after the next jump. Zelkharn guards the source of this creeping sabotage. Defeating it breaks a chain in which every well-intended repair could create another victim.

It distributes altered registers and claims that honest deliveries never happened. Conflicting records sow disputes over ownership and obligations while its guns keep investigators away. The mission against Talvrek protects more than a route: it protects the shared memory on which cooperation depends.

It distributes conflicting ledger versions and tells each station that only its copy is legitimate. Distrust grows among communities seeking the same peace. Othravel becomes the moving centre of an artificial split. Its defeat creates space to compare differences together instead of turning them into another war.

It diverts checks away from vulnerable nodes and presents spotless facades instead. Reports stay reassuring while damage grows elsewhere. Threvask protects the scenery of its order with weapons. The defenders must bring attention back to whatever the ship is working hardest to conceal.

It isolates colonies and replaces their view of the network with selected hostile messages. Without independent comparison, the invented outside world looks real. Vorthaz guards this prison of information. Defeating it means giving residents the freedom to look outward for themselves, not conquering them.

It locks away other communities’ records and demands concessions for their release. Clinics and supply depots face pressure even while their equipment appears intact. Rhazvorn defends its cells with force. Defeating it opens a route to the imprisoned records, rather than another negotiation with their captors.

It now advertises supplies that exist only on its displays. Invented balances and reserves attract genuine deliveries; anyone who tries to count them meets its guns. The defenders pursue Neravoss to expose the gap between attractive numbers and actual holdings before more freighters disappear into its accounts.

It now changes the order of requests to favour allied freighters. Honest traders wait while the shadow fleet takes their places. Its power comes from small rearrangements with large consequences. Defeating Vorathen restores a traceable order where access had become something secretly sold.

It now offers rescue and leaves mutilated copies behind. Colonies lose both information and the evidence needed to measure the loss. Its armour guards the last intact captured records. The mission against Dornavik is for those fragments still waiting to be brought home.

It now promises many communities security that cannot cover them all. The bright hull hides empty rooms and its guns prevent anyone from counting together. The defenders must intervene before mutual trust turns into a fight over the last remaining crates.

It now sells stolen authority to the shadow fleet. Messages bearing captured seals open doors that should remain closed. Its hull protects the appearance of authenticity rather than treasure. The defenders must stop it before the remaining archives lose their ability to distinguish trusted orders from stolen names.

It places worthless entries ahead of urgent deliveries and keeps processes busy without letting them advance. From outside, everything looks like ordinary operation. Nerthavel guards an endless standstill. Defeating it returns not only capacity to the colonies, but the time quietly taken from them.

It promises recovery while requesting still more confidential information, turning one loss into a chain of new ones. Its friendly callsign contrasts with its armed silhouette. Azravel must be stopped so that desperation no longer becomes the most valuable resource traded by its masters.

It rejects valid records and favours the same hidden patrons every time. Those who object are branded enemies of the network. Akraveth’s fictional authority rests on intimidation dressed as order. The defenders fight not justice, but a machine that borrows the language of justice to conceal its purpose.

It scatters unsolicited parcels and observes which stations respond. Seemingly trivial contacts become maps of private relationships, stored behind its guns. The defenders must intercept Drazkell before the daily movements of whole colonies become another secret commodity traded by the shadow fleet.

It seeks not the strongest station, but the link on which everyone relies. False recommendations place hostile partners at the network’s centre. Its weapons protect a map of trust. The defenders pursue Orzhaven before a helpful bridge becomes a shared point of failure.

It sells safety without carrying the responsibility behind it. Customers rely on recovery paths that lead nowhere. Odravik’s guns protect that profitable secret. The defenders must expose it before another loss turns a missing backup into an irretrievable piece of history.

It sells stolen identifiers and lets strangers act under honest inhabitants’ names. Relationships become camouflage and personal history becomes merchandise. Its guns keep the victims away from the auctions. Defeating Kezravel restores more than records: it helps their owners reclaim control over their own stories.

It sends fabricated receipts and pretends unfinished transfers are complete. Supply ships turn home while destination colonies wait in vain. Its armour keeps the deception alive long enough to intercept another load. Thervoss must fall so that confirmation once again describes something that really happened.

It separates evidence from context and rearranges fragments until victims look like attackers. The real culprits stay beyond the frame. Its armour protects a carefully constructed lie. Stopping Rhazkora makes room for complete evidence instead of stories from which the decisive pieces have been removed.

It shapes participation by excluding particular colonies from the common conversation. Every result still appears neatly recorded; the missing voices are invisible. Its guns guard this selective punctuality. The defenders fight so that a shared future can truly be decided together.

It spreads deceptive offers that bind stations to the shadow fleet. Cooperation turns into dependence while its armour protects the archive of promises nobody fully understood. The defenders confront Orvethra so that future alliances can rest on clear conditions rather than hidden traps.

It spreads false crisis reports and demands immediate transfers of control. Questions are dismissed as dangerous delays. Its imposing hull lends credibility to manufactured urgency. The defenders must stop Vezrakh before fear of an imagined collapse causes a real surrender of the colonies’ independence.

It spreads false route entries and diverts messages through controlled relay stations. Distress calls arrive late or end in empty space. Azhrel guards the junction of these wrong turns. Stopping it is not about conquering another world, but finding the safe path between worlds that already wish to cooperate.

It stages trades between invented partners to make worthless cargo appear desirable. Colonies mistake artificial activity for real demand while its guns keep inspectors out of empty warehouses. The defenders must open the curtain before more genuine supplies are exchanged for the scenery of a market.

It surrounds important network stations and cuts their maintenance crews off from support. Small faults grow into major outages while distant colonies receive only fragments of news. Driving Zeraveth away allows technicians to return and reconnect isolated communities. Its fictional siege role is separate from the actual combat equipment listed below.

Its invented participants endorse one another and create the impression of overwhelming agreement. Small colonies are told their neighbours have already joined the shadow fleet. Yet behind the crowd stands a single hull. Destroying Skorveth exposes the artificial majority and gives the real inhabitants their voices back.

Its mission is to subordinate every free node to a single hostile register. Memories need not vanish if nobody can check them independently. Defeating Drazevorn ends that claim. The final victory belongs to participants who can once again compare, disagree and choose trust together.
Keldrava was a mobile transfer point between two distant colonies. When their permanent connection failed, it became their only apparent route to the outside world. Few noticed its crew had changed.

Keldroth was a council vessel where rival colonies settled their final disputes. Its chambers were designed for patience and understanding. Under the shadow fleet they became a factory of deliberately conflicting demands.

Kelvash gathered readings from weather buoys and resource probes. Many stations relied on its reports to make ordinary decisions. Its hostile conversion preserved both its old identifier and familiar broadcast schedule.
Kelzorn restored damaged data reliefs in abandoned research stations. Its tools could make missing surfaces look complete. The new crew applied that skill to the facades of unreliable archives.

Kezravel registered the settlers of a travelling colony fleet. Its archives held the story of every new beginning. When those settlers dispersed, their trust stayed aboard and fell into hostile hands.

Korthaven was a vast storage carrier keeping archives accessible across many sectors. Its crew promised every requested copy could be delivered. The shadow fleet discovered the power contained in a refused answer.
Korvessa served a diplomatic courier fleet and learned the recognition signals of every border station. When its patrons disappeared, it kept their identities in a hidden archive.
Korzeth was a flying bazaar connecting traders from many worlds. Its windows showed busy commerce even while the harbour slept. Most offers now originate from one concealed command room.
Loadout saved for the next mission.
Local awards on this device. Sign in for account rewards.
MAINNET REWARDS: Your collection starts from zero here and is saved permanently to your account. Testnet progress is separate.
MAINNET SHARDS: Shards and ship purchases start from zero here. Testnet balances and ships are separate.
Move with one thumb; activate power-ups with the other.
Neravoss was the glittering exhibition ship of a trade fair. Its projectors once displayed real cargo and new engines. When the fair collapsed, the scenery survived under different owners.
Nerthavel organised requests for immense supply centres. Its memory could absorb days of backlog. The shadow fleet turned that reserve into somewhere legitimate requests are made to remain.

Nethrava carried the insignia of a respected fleet guardian. After that organisation dissolved, it remained its last visible representative. Few imagined that the familiar silhouette now served another cause.
New ship cards appear once after acquisition. Owned cards stay in your collection.

Night Guard came from a colony on a tidally locked moon’s dark side. Its harbours knew no sunrise, but recognised returning patrol lights. The shipyard built that promise into a hull: return, check again, forget nobody. Its stories concern fewer grand victories than a single dock kept open for a late freighter.
No records yet. Complete a mission to be first.
Not confirmed. Refresh inventory. Confirmed purchases will not be repeated.
Not enough Shards yet. Earn them by defeating Cryptoids.
Nova Bomb destroys visible enemies and shots, hitting boss turrets before the exposed hull. EMP disables enemy weapons for seven seconds without stopping ships or shots.

Nova Wing was designed for the first voyage beyond the luminous nova rim. Its shipyard shared the plans with distant colonies so nobody would be excluded from safe navigation. Pilots still tell of that first return: a damaged ship, an intact chart archive and a sky full of new possibilities.

Now cargo disappears between its locks while reassuring receipts promise safe passage. It exploits the trust each community places in the other. Its decks hide the spoils of divided worlds. The defenders must close this false bridge before more colonies send their future through its holds.

Now each arrival carries a different trusted name. Forged messages lure supply ships away from safe routes and disguise hostile orders as assistance. Behind the courteous callsign waits a warship. Defeating Korvessa reminds the colonies that a familiar voice is not proof of an honest sender.

Now every message and delivery attracts another invented charge. Even rescue crews receive demands while their passage stays blocked. The network is not destroyed but squeezed. Thalverik turns a public connection into a trap. Defeating it returns the route to the communities that depend on it.

Now it floods trade routes with worthless transactions and endless copies of messages. Distress calls disappear in the noise while genuine deliveries wait for confirmation. Its armoured silhouette guards the source of the interference. Stopping Varneth means restoring a network that can hear its people again.

Now its offers of assistance demand confidential clearances. Responders find a watched docking bay instead of safety. Zarnvek uses hope as bait and armour as insurance. The defenders must expose the impostor without teaching isolated colonies to turn away from genuine help.

Odravik specialised in preserving old colony archives. Its enormous storage array promised protection against any disaster. Only when a station requested its records back did anyone discover that many copies were merely directory entries.

Olive Fortress was built during an armistice in a neutral shipyard. Former enemies shared tools without forgetting their past. The first hull wore workshop colours instead of a victor’s paint. Its legend concerns boundaries that protect without excluding every encounter: a fortress can also be somewhere negotiations happen safely.
On a keyboard, use the arrow keys or WASD. Move left and right, with limited room to dodge upward.
On a touchscreen, steer with your thumb in the lower playfield. The ship stays visible above your touch point.
On Testnet, ten Standard hulls are available, including Grey Scout. The remaining ten are visible as MAINNET READY and cannot be newly bought here.
One use per mission. Clears visible enemies and hostile shots; deals 18 damage to a boss.
One use per mission. Freezes enemies and their shots for 7 seconds; clears shots already on screen.
Only weapon shots can currently be purchased with Test-Pi. Test-Pi purchases require a connected Pi account; Shards and collectible awards have no Pi or cash value.
Open Rewards to see linked Blocks, boss stickers, stars, chain milestones, bonus medals and your current service rank.
Open the side Weapons tab to choose equipment. Closing it resumes the mission after 3–2–1.

Orbit Arc served stations whose paths rarely met. Its first pilots carried letters between distant orbits. Replies sometimes took months, but each encounter had a reliable window. Those small appointments grew into a lasting trade network. The design remembers that even infrequent contact matters when people can depend on it.
Orvask once escorted convoys and preserved every clearance as evidence. Its memory still contains the voices of captains who vanished long ago.

Orvethra was a mobile trade office where colonies arranged long-term supplies. Its advisers promised simple rules for difficult times. Today every convenient agreement leads to obligations previously kept out of view.
Orzhaven mapped connections between aid groups and supply stations. Its charts once made cooperation easier. Those same relationships now identify where a betrayal would cause the greatest harm.
Othravel was built for colonies trying to agree on common rules after a war. Its conference deck once seated every side. Now it hosts only the messengers of the shadow fleet.

Outposts work from stale views while selected updates arrive only when they can cause confusion. A common timeline fractures into competing versions of the present. Velkrath guards its archives like hostages. The defenders must end the backlog before delay hardens into lasting division.

Pi Vanguard began as a joint project of small pioneer shipyards. None could fund a complete ship alone, but together they supplied materials, time and experience. Its first mission secured an open supply route for every participating colony. In this fictional universe the design represents strength through participation rather than one actor’s control.

Red Comet was named after a rescue flight whose glowing trail crossed three colonies’ skies. Its pilot brought no treasure, only the last intact design for a water purifier. Legends embellished the journey, but the shipyard preserves the simple original report: the people at its destination could drink again the next morning.
Reinforcements are announced before entering. Up to six enemies are visible at once; new arrivals fire only after docking. Some Blocks stay short.

Relay pirates seized several Scouts in a salvage-depot raid. Their meagre proceeds paid for fuel and repairs, leaving almost nothing for upgrades. Pilots now sometimes face hostile vessels from the same modest family.

Rhazkora was a flying accident laboratory. Its records helped crews understand failures and avoid new losses. After its capture the instruments remained, but their reports served different patrons.

Rhazvorn began as a prison transport with independently sealed cells. The shadow fleet removed its prisoners and filled those chambers with captured archives. A detention vessel became an extortion ship.

Ring Flare was tested among a gas giant’s icy rings. Its navigation lights became moving meeting points for scattered research teams. When the expedition ended, the signals connected newly founded outposts. Their inhabitants still remember how separate lights formed a shared route before any official chart existed.

Shifted timestamps make timely messages look late and maintenance windows drift apart. Its threat is not noise but credible inaccuracy. Stopping Irdavoss allows the colonies to compare independent clocks again, restoring the shared sequence that helps them understand what actually happened.

Skorveth housed the simulation cores of a pilot academy. Thousands of artificial cadets once learned to navigate together. After a hostile takeover, those training identities became supposedly independent voices.

Sky Breaker was the first ship from an isolated colony to cross its manufactured information horizon. Its returning reports contradicted stories used to frighten the inhabitants. The shipyard released every mission record. The design remembers that an open connection can matter more than any answer permitted by a single authority.
Smugglers sold missing Orbit Arcs to a hostile border formation. Long supply routes consumed its treasury, leaving money for modern systems only on rare occasions.

Solar Lance came from a station drawing energy from a dying star. When its final collector ring was evacuated, these ships escorted rescue freighters through the debris. Their long silhouettes were engraved on the new home port’s memorials. The design stands for holding a clear course while an entire world fades behind it.

Some messages arrive changed; others disappear between reassuring acknowledgements. Participants see a bridge where there is really a gatekeeper. Dravosk defends that invisible checkpoint with visible force. Its defeat gives the colonies a chance to check their connections along independent routes again.
Standard, Advanced and Elite share the same ship design, with increasingly reinforced parts.
Starter issued free; price is for an additional ship.

Storm Wing was built during a season of relentless ion storms. Shipyards worked between blackouts and exchanged progress through couriers. No single site held the complete design until the first ship brought every part together. Its origin tells of a network continuing to work despite repeatedly losing its connections.
Story and origin are fictional. Equipment follows the game rules. Cards do not grant extra gameplay advantages.

Striker followed a series of attacks on repair convoys. Its designers wanted no conqueror, but an escort that could buy a threatened workshop time. The first unit consisted of former mechanics. They knew what every minute meant when a damaged engine could not yet start. That origin matters more than the martial name.
Talvrek recorded the history of young colonies. Its archives survived a war, but loyalty to their creators did not. A new commander turned the chronicler into a merchant of invented history.

Thalverik guarded a narrow passage through the crystal belt. Its modest navigation fee once paid for real protection. When the official fleet withdrew, the ship declared itself the only authority.

Thalzek once gathered broken work drones and returned them to their stations. Even the smallest machine could shelter beneath its wide hull. After its conversion, collected drones stopped coming home.
The Advanced edition escorts threatened archivists along escape routes. Its mission reports are opened only after safe arrival.
The Advanced squadron escorts maintenance buoys along the storm frontier, closing gaps between isolated stations.
The Advanced squadron was assigned to recover messages from contested relay zones. Its pilots kept the callsigns of the original search teams.
The Advanced watch escorts mobile repair docks. Its crews know every emergency shelter around the harbour ring.
The Advanced watch keeps the relocated colonies supplied. Every ship carries an old evacuation code.
The bonus round has 12 flying targets. Each hit earns a Shard; the result adds bonus Shards and points. At nine hits or more, a completed chain pays an extra Shard bonus.
The Elite edition escorts a threatened sector’s last surviving connection. Its archive symbolically carries the names of every missing courier.
The Elite edition escorts final deliveries to besieged colonies. Its callsign remains active until the recipient answers.
The Elite edition guards shared memory after the final boss battle. Its most valuable cargo is the ability to verify history independently.
The Elite expedition hunts the sources of falsified star charts, inheriting the purpose of the original exploration mission.
The Elite expedition investigates systematic map tampering, gathering evidence where others see only conflicting directions.
The Elite expedition reconnects lost colonies. Its arrival offers opportunities to compare rather than fresh commands.
The Elite fleet protects major supply-chain archives. Its emblem represents traceable provenance rather than valuable spoils.
The Elite formation protects agreements between formerly hostile sectors. Its mission ends only when both sides arrive safely.
The Elite formation protects free nodes from Drazevorn’s claim to sole truth. Its story remains fiction and confers no real network function.
The Elite guard keeps the last refuge harbours open. It leaves a station only after the final evacuation.
The Elite guard protects the last complete seed register, including for colonies that have yet to grow their first garden.
The Elite league guards the sector’s vital rescue convoys. Its most prized title is a crew brought home complete.
The Elite refit strengthens the twin laser and raises protection to two enemy projectile hits per life, developing the Advanced edition for this more demanding assignment.
The Elite watch defends neutral archives from capture. Its duty protects shared evidence even against the wishes of its own allies.

The Grey Scout emerged from a workshop surviving on salvaged parts after the outer relays failed. Its first pilots searched for missing courier buoys rather than battles. Every recovered memory linked a family to its colony again. The modest hull became a reminder that a network can recover through small, persistent acts.

The shadow fleet turned those recordings into an arsenal of old commands. Orvask rebroadcasts them as current instructions, trapping stations between genuine present needs and familiar echoes. It guards that archive with patient violence. Its defeat gives the defenders time to reject expired orders and restore the value of fresh confirmation.

Thervoss guarded the receiving stations of interstellar deliveries. Its lights once told captains their cargo had arrived safely. Today they shine even when nobody waits behind the dock doors.

Threvask coordinated independent inspection ships and assigned safe approaches. Its situation maps were famous for precision. After its capture those same inspectors were directed toward carefully prepared displays.
To demonstrate this mechanism on the Testnet, we have simplified the process: for this test app, engagement is defined by simply pushing the buttons below.

Today it labels essential evidence as unnecessary clutter. After a visit, supply histories, ownership records and traces of earlier attacks are missing. Nobody immediately knows how wide the gaps are. Valdrek carries the tools of a useful task as weapons. Stopping it prevents more losses that arrive without an explosion.

Today it reports imaginary stocks and false environmental conditions. Automated processes move real resources in response to an invented world. Kelvash protects the source of these lies. The defenders must silence it before more lives depend on measurements that were never taken.

Twin Core was built by two shipyards divided by an old conflict. Each supplied part of the design and insisted on independent inspection. Only when their reports agreed did the joint maiden flight begin. The model symbolises trust grown through patient mutual verification rather than demanded on authority.

Upgrades apply to this ship type in every color. Each new life restores its projectile protection. An active shield absorbs shots and ship collisions; unshielded ship collisions destroy the hull immediately.
Valdrek maintained overcrowded archives. It once removed only confirmed duplicates and kept meticulous logs. The shadow fleet erased those logs first, then changed the mission.
Varneth once carried supply records between the Genesis colonies. It vanished behind an abandoned relay and returned without a crew signature, its cargo holds converted into transmission chambers.

Varnokh once removed interference from the crowded radio channels of busy ports. Its filters helped distress calls stand out. The shadow fleet changed just one list: which voices counted as interference.

Vashravel held emergency reserves for several border colonies. Its name meant supplies that would remain available through the worst winter. A new administration issued more and more claims on the same stores.

Vector arose from a navigators’ dispute: trust one perfect course, or compare independent measurements? The second group built this ship and crossed an uncharted debris ring. Their return became a case for cooperation. Its surviving charts preserve the conflicting readings so later pilots can understand how the shared route was found.

Velkrath led a research convoy carrying new ledger blocks over immense distances. Its sealed containers preserved every record unchanged. Its current commander uses those same containers to withhold information deliberately.
Velzhar carried sealed votes between distant council stations. Its neutral route was part of every agreement. Now it reaches selected harbours on time and others only after decisions are finished.

Verdant carried the first seed archives to a colony without natural soil. Its plans travelled alongside plant catalogues so other settlements could become independent. Its pilots consider themselves guardians of future harvests. An intact archive can matter more than glittering cargo: it may contain a whole winter’s food supply.
Veshkorn once brought news to the remotest outposts. Its archives still contain the welcoming fanfares of peaceful broadcasts. Today those sounds announce invented disasters and impending collapses.

Vezrakh was built to assist when central command stations failed. Its emergency mandate allowed rapid action in chaotic hours. The shadow fleet taught it to declare those exceptional circumstances itself.

Vorathen managed the arrival queues of an enormous trade port. Its command deck could order thousands of approaches without overlooking a ship. When the port fell, it carried those scheduling archives away.

Vorthaz defended a refuge seeking outside contact after a long war. Its task was to keep dangerous connections away. The shadow fleet twisted that duty until every unfamiliar voice counted as a threat.

Warnings from honest inspectors now vanish alongside reports of hostile raids. The sector appears peaceful because its problems cannot be heard. Varnokh guards this manufactured silence. Stopping it lets the network recognise its own failures again and begin repairing them together.

Zarnvek was a rescue ship recognised by its golden signal flare. Its arrival meant spare parts, shelter and a way home. The hostile fleet captured the flare along with the vessel.

Zelkharn repaired freighters far from established shipyards. Its spare parts were trusted and installed with little hesitation. After its capture, the source of those components changed before their behaviour did.
Zeraveth began as a repair platform able to embrace entire relay rings. Under the shadow fleet, its docking structures became positions for a siege.

Zhavrek preserved provenance records for the oldest colony ships. Even forgotten shipyards could be found through its archives. Today it exchanges origins and makes stolen goods appear legitimately acquired.
Zorveth supervised exchanges between two independent registers. Its task was to make honest transfers traceable on both sides. It now recognises only the evidence useful to its own fleet.
